source.title: Scaling Laws for Embedding Dimension in Information Retrieval
source.authors: J. Killingback; Mahta Rafiee; M. Manas; Hamed Zamani

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study examines analogous scaling behavior in dense information retrieval, rather than language-model pretraining loss, and reports its own results on embedding dimension, model size, and retrieval performance.
record.gate_note: The paper measures dense-retrieval contrastive entropy and ranking metrics, not held-out language-model pretraining cross-entropy. It varies embedding dimension and encoder parameter count, and considers inference FLOPs; it does not test token-count scaling or a training-compute-optimal allocation. The reported results bear on V6's retrieval-performance predictability and V7's fit/setup dependence and departures from a simple scaling pattern.
record.test_reason: New setting: dense retrievers fine-tuned from BERT and Ettin encoders. Its joint law fits contrastive-entropy (a fine-tuned task loss) as a power law in parameter count N. That bears on V5's fine-tuning regime, and the eval-set dependence of the fitted exponent bears on V7. The main axis, embedding dimension, is not parameters, tokens or compute, so those rows fit no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Correction: the authors attribute the less predictable out-of-domain behaviour to models trained with knowledge distillation (the BERT recipe), not to 'distilled BERT models'. They also conclude that a larger model with a smaller projected embedding often beats a smaller model with a larger embedding, and that ANN scoring favours larger embedding dimensions.
record.recipe_differences: This is a dense-retrieval study of contrastive entropy and ranking metrics, varying embedding dimension and encoder parameter count; it does not reproduce language-model held-out pretraining-loss scaling.
record.method_sensitivity: Fit and behavior vary across model family, model size, evaluation dataset, and training recipe. Out-of-domain behavior is less predictable; BERT on Paper Retrieval can worsen at larger dimensions. The authors use nonlinear least squares via SciPy curve_fit.

fits_no_version.finding: Contrastive entropy falls as a saturating power law in embedding dimension (α 0.018-0.977, mostly R²>0.95). The fit is poorer for the largest Ettin on MSMARCO Dev (R²=0.53).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Retrieval loss scales as a power law in embedding dimension, with an irreducible floor.

fits_no_version.finding: Out of domain, entropy vs dimension is erratic and ticks up at large dimension for BERT (distillation-trained) on Paper Retrieval, but not for Ettin.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Embedding-dimension scaling holds less predictably out of domain.

fits_no_version.finding: RR@10 and R@1000 rise with embedding dimension for BERT on MSMARCO Dev; the trend is less smooth than for entropy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Embedding-dimension gains in contrastive entropy carry over to ranking metrics.

fits_no_version.finding: Under a fixed per-query inference-FLOPs budget, the optimal model size and embedding dimension both grow with budget (Fig 6, from the BERT TREC fit).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inference-compute-optimal allocation scales encoder size and embedding dimension jointly.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval
record.problems: The main evidence is contrastive entropy, which the study uses as a proxy for retrieval performance. The out-of-domain and ranking-metric results are presented in figures without numerical values in the text. TREC DL Combined has 150 queries; the authors note lower fit quality for the largest Ettin, especially on MSMARCO Dev.
record.rows_left_out: Individual plotted values and checkpoint-specific out-of-domain curves in Figure 4, and per-checkpoint ranking metric curves in Figure 5, are not transcribed because the text does not assign numerical values to them; the reported family-level descriptions are retained in r31-r33.

untested.parts: Held-out LM pretraining loss vs parameters, tokens or compute.
Training-compute-optimal N/token split. The paper's allocation is over inference FLOPs between encoder and scoring.
Token or training-compute scaling in fine-tuning; other modalities; repeated data. The model-size law is fit only on aligned eval sets, not out of domain.
No LM downstream-task prediction from scale or pretraining loss. The ranking metrics are only checked against embedding dimension.
Fitting-method, parameter-counting and schedule choices are not varied.

missing.what: Text says larger models beat smaller ones at equal embedding dimension, with diminishing gains (e.g. BERT-L4-H512 at 8k dims is worse than L8-H512 at 256 dims)

record.verdict_notes: Contrastive entropy is a fine-tuned retrieval loss, not LM pretraining loss, so only the model-size term is mapped to V5. Checkpoints are selected for the best eval entropy, which flatters the fits. Section 4.1 says noise would 'increase R²'; this is evidently a typo for decrease.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out pretraining loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or training compute.
The study does not fit on small runs and test predictions on runs orders of magnitude larger.
It considers an inference-FLOPs budget for retrieval, not training-compute-optimal parameter and token allocation.
It does not isolate depth, width, or other architecture changes at fixed parameter count.
It tests dense text retrieval, not other modalities or the listed training regimes.
Tests retrieval performance across embedding dimensions and encoder sizes; does not test language-model downstream tasks or prediction from pretraining loss.
Tests fit variation across retrieval models and evaluation sets, and less predictable out-of-domain behavior; does not test language-model loss exponents or training-compute-optimal splits.

rows.subject: BERT family
rows.operation_detail: Fit a joint contrastive-entropy scaling law using model size and embedding dimension.
rows.note: The joint fit is reported for the BERT family and this evaluation set.
rows.check: Joint law L=A/D^α+B/N^β+δ. The N term is a parameter power law for the fine-tuned loss. BERT checkpoints span only about 4M-109M parameters.

rows.subject: BERT family
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate embedding-dimension scaling on Paper Retrieval.
rows.measure: Contrastive entropy; the text reports that several models' entropy rises at larger dimensions, especially on this task.
rows.note: The text does not identify which individual BERT checkpoints show the uptick; it says the pattern is especially common for BERT on Paper Retrieval.
rows.check: Out-of-domain entropy vs embedding dimension: an embedding-dimension axis, so no version. Figure only.

rows.subject: Ettin family
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate embedding-dimension scaling on out-of-domain retrieval tasks.
rows.measure: Contrastive entropy; authors report generally decreasing entropy as dimensions increase and no Ettin uptick like the BERT Paper Retrieval pattern, while describing OOD behavior overall as erratic.
rows.note: Family-level description; plotted individual values are not transcribed.
rows.check: Out-of-domain entropy vs embedding dimension; no version. Figure only.

rows.subject: BERT family
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate ranking performance as embedding dimension is scaled.
rows.measure: Authors report that performance improvement holds as embedding dimension increases; the trend is clearer for R@1000 than RR@10.
rows.note: The text describes the family-level trend; plotted values vary by model and are not given numerically.
rows.check: Ranking metrics vs embedding dimension for one family on one dataset, so no version. This is a check that contrastive entropy tracks ranking metrics.

relationships.condition: Dense-retrieval fine-tuning of BERT (4-109M) and Ettin (17M-1B) encoders, aligned eval sets MSMARCO Dev and TREC DL
relationships.reason: Joint laws with an N^-β term fit contrastive entropy with R² 0.975-0.997 (r27-r30). The range spans under two orders of magnitude.
relationships.display_finding: Joint laws containing an N^-β term fitted contrastive entropy with R²=0.975–0.997 over less than two orders of magnitude.

relationships.condition: Same joint laws compared across eval set and model family/training recipe
relationships.reason: The model-size exponent β shifts with eval set and family: BERT 1.247 vs 0.961, Ettin 0.805 vs 0.588 (r27-r30).
relationships.display_finding: Model-size β differed across evaluation sets, taking values 1.247 versus 0.961 for BERT and 0.805 versus 0.588 for Ettin.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Aligned retrieval evaluation on MSMARCO Dev and TREC DL Combined
reader_labels.reason: Dimension-only and joint fits generally have high R², and the authors report improvements with increasing embedding dimension; ranking metrics also improve in the tested BERT subset (r01-r30, r33).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Out-of-domain Paper Retrieval and Legal QA
reader_labels.reason: The authors describe scaling as less predictable out of domain and report entropy increases at larger dimensions for some BERT Paper Retrieval settings (r31-r32).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Dimension-only fits and joint fits across retrieval families and evaluation sets
reader_labels.reason: Fit parameters differ across datasets, model families, and individual encoder sizes; fit quality is also notably lower for the largest Ettin on MSMARCO Dev (r01-r30).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Out-of-domain retrieval, especially BERT on Paper Retrieval
reader_labels.reason: The authors say out-of-domain scaling is less predictable and report dimension-related entropy upticks for some BERT models (r31-r32).
